questions.q: What is the definition of the mode in a data set?
questions.a: The mode is the value that occurs with the highest frequency in a data set. A wrong answer like "the average" shows the student is confusing mode with mean, which requires calculation rather than simple counting.

questions.q: If a list of shoe sizes is 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7, why is 6 the mode?
questions.a: 6 is the mode because it appears 3 times, which is more frequent than any other size. If a student says "because it is in the middle," they are confusing mode with median.

questions.q: Find the mode of these marks in a test: 10, 15, 10, 20, 10, 15.
questions.a: 1. List the unique values: 10, 15, 20. 2. Count frequencies: 10 appears 3 times, 15 appears 2 times, 20 appears 1 time. 3. Compare counts: 3 is the largest. 4. Identify mode: 10. A student who says 15 likely miscounted or skipped the last 10.

questions.q: If a cricket player scores 5, 10, 5, 20, 5, 10 runs in six matches, which score is the mode?
questions.a: The mode is 5. It appears 3 times, while 10 appears twice and 20 appears once. A student answering 5 and 10 together is confusing the concept with multimodal data, which is outside our current scope.

questions.q: Is the mode always the largest number in a data set? Explain.
questions.a: No, the mode is the most frequent number, not the biggest one. For example, in 2, 2, 2, 9, 9, the mode is 2, even though 9 is the largest number. A "Yes" answer reveals a misunderstanding of "frequency" versus "value magnitude."

questions.q: Create a small data set of 5 numbers where the mode is 4.
questions.a: A correct set would be 4, 4, 4, 1, 2. A poor answer like 4, 1, 2, 3, 5 shows a failure to ensure 4 appears more frequently than other numbers.
